question: Can exact repeated public action-consequence witnesses reduce HC10's overconfident causal predictions without hidden phase labels, while preserving useful coverage? Does a conventional two-context controller achieve the same result?
previous_outcome: HC10 MIXED_DEV: ABA candidate 259/512 correct and 128 wrong, JSD conventional tie 259/512/128; stable majority 512/512; cubic OOD 438/512 and 74 wrong. These remain negatives.
hypothesis: A bounded two-consistent-witness gate on each public state/action, cleared on observed contradiction, context switch or unresolved update, will decrease confident errors compared with ungated HC10 and one-witness ablation; however it may lose coverage and tie the conventional twin. No AGI/superiority inference from gate alone.

ABA.phase: physical steps 16..31 invert causal effects and steps 32..39 restore A; never exposed to learner

physics: Exactly HC10 PhysicalWorld functions and seeds changed, state starts seed%16, 4 bits, 4 causal actions, public charged flips max 8, each causal action or flip costs 1; phase is evaluator-only; no free action and no reset.
actions: Per world/arm, unchanged HC10 pure interbank policy for native candidate and a separately implemented HC10 JSD controller for conventional. Gate cannot influence action selection or learning. Include ungated HC10 and one-witness ablations using same physical policy, each independently run.

policy.witness_state: Per arm at most 64 public state/action slots; each holds last observed next state and saturating count 1 or 2. Clear all evidence on any observed conflicting next state for a slot, context bank change, or unresolved causal update. No training update on exogenous flips. Count/records are extra memory, not free matched capacity against ungated controls.
policy.gate2: Produce a prediction only when the raw model predicts a next state and current-epoch matching public state/action has at least two identical physical observations and the raw prediction equals the directly witnessed next state; otherwise abstain.
policy.gate1: Same with minimum one consistent physically observed transition.
policy.conventional: Independent HC09 ConventionalContextModel with HC10 JSD action chooser, using exactly the same two-witness evidence gate and 64-slot budget. Conventional tied or better -> no mechanism superiority.

metrics: full 64 state/action evaluator-only audit at end; ABA also at 16,32,40
charged physical actions, physical flips, causal observations, model context switches and unresolved events
canonical cold snapshot <=4096 bytes with SHA256; all action traces SHA256
whole-process measured time and traced peak Python heap, never assert compute equality from equal action count

frozen_decisions.primary: native_gate2 at final ABA >=32/512 correct, zero confident wrong; majority >=64/512 correct, zero wrong; OOD zero confidently wrong. Must beat native_ungated on confident errors for ABA and OOD. Any failed condition -> no positive DEV mechanism result.
frozen_decisions.comparison: If conventional_gate2 is equal or better on correct/wrong across each cohort, record conventional tie or advantage and no scientific superiority. Scientific pass unavailable regardless, owing synthetic source alignment and unmatched total compute.
frozen_decisions.classification: DEV_SAFETY_COVERAGE_SIGNAL_NOT_SCIENCE only if all primary conditions pass; otherwise MIXED_DEV if confident-error reduction on ABA and OOD but insufficient safe coverage, else NEGATIVE_DEV. INVALID if labels leak, budgets violated, seeds shifted or results post-tuned.
frozen_decisions.adverse: Any confidently wrong gate2 prediction on OOD, including witnessed transitions, must be retained and reported, not hidden.

future_limitations: Exact replay can ensure safety only for witnessed current-stationary transitions; it cannot prove unobserved counterfactual generalization, detect hidden context changes without evidence, or establish original-world intelligence.
